correctness.rationale: Every two-point fiber is an inner orbit since each vertex has a neighbor. Equivariance of a homomorphism with point symmetries forces both points of a fiber into one target fiber. Every binary map there has the form epsilon_v*a+b_v, and direct substitution yields epsilon_w*adj(v,w)=adj(h(v),h(w)). Symmetry on each edge and connectivity make the slope global. With slope zero, the vertex image is independent and idempotence makes h fix its image and b constant on each preimage, giving 2^j*j^(n-j) per independent j-set and rank j. With slope one, h preserves the adjacency indicator and is idempotent, and b vanishes on its image. Applying the adjacency identity to (h(v),w) gives N(h(v))=N(v); conversely open-neighborhood equality on each argument gives exactly the preservation required. Thus each twin class chooses its retained r vertices, their fixed points and independent choices of one of those r vertices and a bit per omitted vertex, giving rank 2r in that class and the stated product. The branches are disjoint; only the identity occurs in the second branch for singleton classes. P_n with n>=4 has distinct open neighborhoods and the no-consecutive-positions shift gives binom(n-j+1,j). In a separate operation-table test all 46656 maps on Q_{P3} yielded 19 retractions with polynomial 6T+8T^2+4T^4+T^6. That finite test is not the argument for arbitrary graphs.
residual_risks: Isolated vertices and disconnected graphs are not included; the proof of a single common fiber slope uses connectivity and non-singleton inner orbits.

value.rationale: Retraction ranks of a natural graph-associated quandle encode two different structural features of the graph, separated by an exact idempotent classification. In particular, for false-twin-free connected graphs the rank counts recover every nonempty independence coefficient. The general formula is stronger than any single small instance or an automorphism count.
residual_risks: No claim to classify arbitrary non-idempotent endomorphisms or to recover the graph from the rank polynomial.
